Per-step cost has a pixel-proportional compute part plus a bandwidth-bound or small-channel part on the 31×31 stem maps. The tip (E036) scored 5.31 s and 0.7532 on seeds 0–2. Fresh-seed reruns read 0.7525 (E038) and 0.7497 (E043, same commit). So 3-seed noise is about 0.15–0.25 pp, and the population mean is about 0.752, only about 0.2 pp above the 0.75 bar. Time noise is about ±0.03 s, with E043 showing drift even at an identical commit.

Mechanisms I believe:
1. Accuracy rises slowly with total optimizer steps, at about 1.5–2.5 s/pp. Every pure time cut (E020, E031, E040, E041, E037, E045) bought time at a roughly dial-like rate. The exceptions are the systems and truncation levers.
2. Early low resolution is nearly free (E026, E033). The 32 px tail and the 3×3 final-map regime carry accuracy (E011, E018, E024).
3. Backward truncation saves more time than its MAC share (E028, E034, E036, E046). E046's group-2 freeze for the last 10% saved about 0.24 s, about 4.5% of the run, at only about −0.1 pp on 3 seeds. That is a second backward-truncation win, so memory-bound and small-map backward work is expensive. The dose is nonlinear: E037's 60% freeze lost about 0.4 pp, while E042 was neutral. Late freezes are cheap and early ones are costly.
4. Averaging, LS, warm-up, Lookahead-interval, BN-recalibration and batch-split tweaks (E025, E029, E030, E032, E044, E045) are null or negative. The recipe sits at a narrow local optimum, so I shade non-systems changes by about −0.1 pp.
5. Systems-only math-identical work gives about 1–2% each (E035). Bit-reproducibility is imperfect (E043).
6. wd ×0.5 helped about 0.2 pp (E016). Muon's gain is confounded with batch size and an RNG re-draw.
7. Sample dropping (E031) costs about 0.3 pp for about 0.6 s, which is no better than the epoch dial.

forecasts.reason: Diagnostic with no recipe change. Time and accuracy are just the tip's rerun noise. The profile will likely show the stem and non-GEMM kernels are over-weighted.
About 5% fewer steps buys about 0.1 s and costs about 0.1–0.15 pp. That is roughly dial-like and sits within noise. The 3-seed mean probably falls below 0.753.
Padding Cin to 32 may speed up conv1 by about 1%, or do nothing if cuDNN already pads internally. Math is identical, but the RNG-dependent path is unchanged, so accuracy stays at tip noise.

cruxes: Is the tip's true population mean about 0.752 or about 0.7535? That decides whether any further time cut can stay above the 0.75 bar on 40 seeds.
Does the group-2 freeze (E046) stay neutral in accuracy on fresh seeds 13–32 and extend to a longer dose (15%) without a cliff?
Where does the stem's time go: conv1 with Cin=24 inefficiency, or bandwidth-bound pool and elementwise work? If it is conv1 padding, I073 is a free win.
